text:
Maria Chen: RFC merged. Quick decision needed: where should panel-level RBAC & projection live? Query-service pushdown vs panel-controller pull/cache.

Kevin Patel: I prefer pushdown for perf, but worry it hard-couples product rules into query service.

Sophia Li: Panel-controller gives experimentation flexibility, but adds a network hop and surface for SLOs. Degrade plan needed.

Oliver Grant: Cache invalidation is harder if we move checks outwards. Query layer is currently the source of truth for tenant scoping.

Arnav Singh: Summary of tradeoffs: pushdown -> better cold latency and cache locality; pull -> composability, simpler UI rollouts, decoupled contracts.

Maria Chen: Proposed hybrid: keep tenant_id and coarse scoping in QueryService; push per-panel projections and feature RBAC into PanelController. Try to preserve cache hit rate.

Kevin Patel: Implementation sketch:
- QueryService: enforce tenant scoping + prefilters for flagged panels
- PanelController: request tenant-scoped payloads, apply panel projection & RBAC
- Cache: panel-side LRU keyed by (panel_id, permissions-hash, contract_version)

Sophia Li: What about join-heavy panels that depend on DB row-level security? Post-filtering could leak aggregate signals.

Oliver Grant: Add an explicit opt-in flag on the panel contract: requires_strict_rls. When true, QueryService will apply server-side RLS and return prefiltered rows.

Maria Chen: Draft panel contract (minimal):
```
panel_id: string
contract_version: string
requires_strict_rls: bool
projection: [string]
allow_partial: bool
```

Arnav Singh: Add permissions-hash as part of the cache key and require contract_version bump for rollout changes.

Kevin Patel: Ops notes: tie cache invalidations to permission-change events (user role updates) and consider aggressive TTL for high-risk panels.

Sophia Li: Before rollout we need metrics: p50/p95 panel latency, panel cache hit rate, permission-change invalidations/sec, auth-fail vs projection-fail counts.

Maria Chen: I'll own a 1-week spike to implement panel-side LRU prototype + metric hooks, then a canary on a low-risk dashboard.

Oliver Grant: I'll build a harness to compare requires_strict_rls=true vs false under realistic joins.

Arnav Singh: I'll update the RFC with the contract, rollout plan, and an ops checklist.

DeployBot: feature-branches merged to staging at 2026-03-12T14:34Z (build #4821)

Maria Chen: If no objections by EOD tomorrow we start the spike. Thanks all :thumbsup:
